The team note's claim is a real objection, but it's not the most powerful one, because it only shows the calculus is impractical, and a utilitarian can reply with rough estimates. The stronger refutation is the commensurability objection: if pleasures and pains differ in kind, as Mill argued, there is no common unit to sum, so the calculus has no determinate output even in principle.
